title: Pendulum, 100 cm

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with known physics (a school practical: true length 1.00 m, g = 9.81 m/s²)

slow_motion.evidence: No captions, narration, or visual cues indicate slow motion

subjects.description: small orange spherical bob hanging from a thin string

observation.what_happens: An orange ball suspended by a thin string swings side-to-side below a fixed mount. It moves from right of centre toward centre and continues oscillating side-to-side for the duration of the clip.

calibration.note: white paper sheet = 0.297 m (Standard A4 sheet long side) spans 130 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: white paper sheet = 0.297 m (Standard A4 sheet long side) spans 130 px in SAM's mask, known to ±6%
pendulum length L = 0.957 m, measured from the radius of the swing with the ruler: hold L fixed and measure g
reasoning: Theta shows a ~0.17 rad sinusoid with ~2 s period on a 0.957 m circular arc, matching L=0.957 m pendulum timing, with only slight amplitude loss over 5 s. Candidates go from small-angle and exact ideal motion to linear viscous and quadratic aerodynamic damping to identify the cause of the slow decay and best extrapolate.

caveats: Scale comes from the A4 sheet width and carries systematic error into gravity.
String length was held fixed from the swing radius, so gravity depends on that choice.
Linear and quadratic drag predict almost the same here, so drag type is not firmly settled.
critique.finding: The orange ball swings like a true pendulum pulled by gravity with g = {g} on a string of length {L}. A tiny bit of air drag with strength {kq} slowly steals its swing.
critique.headline: Orange ball swings on string, air barely slows it.
critique.why_it_won: It lets faster swings lose a little extra energy, so it follows the shrinking peaks better than steady linear damping.

headline: Orange ball swings on string, air barely slows it.
finding: The orange ball swings like a true pendulum pulled by gravity with g = 9.39 ± 0.56 m/s² on a string of length 0.957 m. A tiny bit of air drag with strength 0.0697 ± 0.0073 1/rad slowly steals its swing.

eyeball.law_in_words: Small-angle simple pendulum period T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) with L scaled from the 0.297 m paper sheet, with peak amplitude envelope decaying as 1/theta linear in time due to quadratic air-drag torque proportional to angular-velocity squared with coefficient kq.
